journal:
I should have known better to be honest, I had this rotation that I used to do in downtown back when I had the sausage cart, I remember on Friday's I used to park down near the edge of quite a nice piazza and you'd often get quite a bit of traffic after work right as everyone was either heading home or getting ready to meet up with friends and family. Fridays were always good for business, so I always used to pack extra meat as i'd often sell out.

Well i'd usually stick around until about 7, and I remember there was this scruffy looking dog I saw onece, poor thing looks so sorry for itself; very gentle though, and would always lay down around thirty feet from the cart, anyway, I ended up taking pity and poor thing, it clearly had no owner, so If I had a day when I didn't manage to sell out, i'd feed it a few of leftovers before I packed up and left. As you can imagine, this ended up going on for quite a while. Every Friday he'd show up, lay in the same spot, and wait patiently until I started packing away.

After about a month or so I noticed he would start sitting slightly closer each week, it wasn't by much, but just enough I started to take notice. In the end he got so close I was worried he'd start driving away business, so I decided one week to buy a small dog bed to put behind the stand, if he was going to wait all day for a meal, at the very least he'd be out of sight of the customers behind the cart.

I'm not sure how old he was, but for the next four years he'd sit with me, every friday, and was good company to keep on the slow days.
prompt: Low at pavement level beside a street food cart at night, the orange glow of the grill falls on a scruffy dog's face as lays down and eats a sausage off the floor

music.why: A gentle, slowly built bond between a street vendor and a stray dog on Friday evenings, warm grill glow at night, calls for soft, close and heartfelt music.
